subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw add native backup exclude-pattern controls now, and which default exclusions, protected paths, and exclude-file trust rules should become part of the core backup CLI contract?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but the permanent behavior balances archive size, sensitive-file avoidance, restore completeness, JSON/manifest compatibility, and local exclude-file trust, which requires maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a maintainer rewrite of it to settle flags, defaults, protected paths, manifest behavior, and proof before landing.

options.title: Narrow to explicit excludes first
options.body: Accept only repeatable `--exclude` and explicit `--exclude-file` support while deferring smart defaults and auto-discovery until restore/security expectations are settled.

options.title: Decline native excludes for now
options.body: Keep built-in backup coarse, document the current scope, and point optional backup strategies such as Keep My Claw to ClawHub after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a maintainer rewrite of it to settle flags, defaults, protected paths, manifest behavior, and proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and hardened the original backup CLI surface, making them the strongest available routing candidate for the core backup contract decision.
